original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let I be a complete intersection ideal in the polynomial ring K[x1, ..., xn], where n is arbitrary. Must the Artinian quotient K[x1, ..., xn]/I always have the weak Lefschetz property, and does it perhaps always have the strong Lefschetz property as well?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Question 2.1 (Complete Intersections): “Does every complete intersection ideal I ⊆ K[x1, ..., xn], in any number of variables, has the WLP (or even the SLP)?” The paper immediately describes this as “the main open problem concerning Lefschetz properties for complete intersections.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core target right: it works over a field of characteristic zero, asks about complete intersections in K[x1, ..., xn] for arbitrary n, places the question on the quotient algebra, and asks first for the weak Lefschetz property and then for the stronger possibility of the strong Lefschetz property. That is exactly the scope of the paper’s official formulation in Section 2, Question 2.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
missing_details: The paper’s question lives in the graded Artinian setting, so I should be specified as a homogeneous complete intersection ideal in the standard graded polynomial ring S = K[x1, ..., xn]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should say explicitly that A = S/I is Artinian; equivalently here, I is generated by a homogeneous regular sequence of length n (so ht(I) = n). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

The draft does not define the weak Lefschetz property: there should exist a linear form ℓ in A1 such that multiplication ×ℓ : Ai → A{i+1} has maximal rank for every degree i. This definition is implicit in the paper’s surrounding discussion of WLP for Artinian graded algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

The draft does not define the strong Lefschetz property: there should exist a linear form ℓ in A1 such that ×ℓ^d : Ai → A{i+d} has maximal rank for every i and every d ≥ 1. The paper explicitly contrasts WLP with this stronger SLP version in Question 2.1 and the surrounding paragraph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
The universal quantifiers should be explicit: for every integer n ≥ 1 and for every Artinian homogeneous complete intersection I ⊆ K[x1, ..., xn]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

The paper’s official phrasing is a sharp yes/no problem (“WLP, or even SLP”), so the tentative wording “perhaps always” should be replaced by the exact stronger alternative asked in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
refined_question: For every integer n ≥ 1, let S = K[x1, ..., xn] be the standard graded polynomial ring over a field K of characteristic 0, and let I ⊂ S be a homogeneous complete intersection ideal such that A = S/I is Artinian (equivalently, I is generated by a homogeneous regular sequence of length n). Must A have the weak Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that ×ℓ : Ai → A{i+1} has maximal rank for every i? More strongly, must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that ×ℓ^d : Ai → A{i+d} has maximal rank for every i and every d ≥ 1?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2, Question 2.1, not the narrower follow-up questions. Section 2 first fixes the standing assumption that the field has characteristic zero unless otherwise stated, then reviews the known cases for complete intersections in two variables, Artinian height three complete intersections, and monomial complete intersections, and from exactly that context poses Question 2.1. The next sentence says this should be regarded as “the main open problem concerning Lefschetz properties for complete intersections,” which confirms that Question 2.1 is the nearest official formulation your draft is trying to capture. The page number 212 is inferred from the chapter range pp. 211–225 together with a snippet showing Question 2.1 on the chapter’s second page. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))
